question: Each year, under Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/13511 the Commission assesses whether Member States are: (i) under migratory pressure; (ii) at risk thereof; or (iii) facing a significant migratory situation. This determines access to the Solidarity Pool and calibrated contributions (relocation, financial, operational). 1.

What quantitative indicators (with thresholds), qualitative criteria and weighting formulas govern this classification, and can the Commission specify parameters including: unauthorised crossings and asylum applications (absolute/per capita); secondary movements; reception capacity relative to GDP per capita and population; external border exposure metrics; returns executed; vulnerability indices?

For the latest 2025 classification (Annual Report): which concrete datasets were used (e.g. Eurostat, Frontex, national authorities, and with what reference periods and extraction dates), and how are raw figures aggregated into composite scores, and how do these scores compare across individual Member States?

How does the Commission ensure methodological consistency and comparability across Member States when applying these classification criteria, and what mechanisms exist for Member States to challenge or seek clarification on their classification?
Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of 14 May 2024 on asylum and migration management (ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1351/oj).
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2026) For the purpose of the assessment pursuant to Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/13511, the Commission developed an evidence-based methodology on the basis of the elements listed in Article 9, in particular paragraph (3), point (a) and Article 10(2), points (a) to (k) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351.

The aggregation of these elements is explained in a Commission Staff Working Document2. The quantitative data was provided by the Member States via the Union Agencies and Eurostat, pursuant to Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 in line with a common definition and methodology.

The data, which undergo regular quality checks and provide a solid basis for the assessment of the migratory situation in the Union and the Member States, are listed in an annex to the Annual Report3 in a dedicated Commission Staff Working Document4 that was transmitted to the European Parliament.

The assessment covers a 12-month period from 1 July year n-1 to 30 June year n (for the first report: from 1 July 2024 to 30 June 2025) to identify Member States under migratory pressure and Member States at risk of migratory pressure, respectively.

To identify Member States facing a significant migratory situation, the assessment covers the period 1 July year n-5 to 30 June year n (for the first report: 1 July 2020 to 30 June 2025). The results of the first assessment are set out in the Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/23235. The methodology was developed in consultation with Member States and is applied consistently across Member States.
A Member State can ask for a reassessment pursuant to Articles 59, 61 and 62 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351.
1 Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 14 May 2024 on asylum and
migration management, amending Regulations (EU) 2021/1147 and (EU) 2021/1060 and repealing Regulation (EU) No 604/2013, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:L_202401351.

2 Commission Staff Working Document, Methodology for the purposes of Commission implementing decision pursuant to Article 11 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1351 of the European Parliament and of the Council, SWD(2025) 792 final, https://home-affairs.ec.europa.eu/document/download/80637837-e569-4896-98f22e8b92abf66e_en?filename=Methodology_en.pdf.
